### Observed differences

- Five activities became universal. In the earlier window, A22 ran in about 47 of 100 traces and each of A31, A32, A37 and A38 in about 54 of 100; in the later window, all five run in every trace, each exactly once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A22 and the four activities A31, A32, A37, A38 were strict alternatives before and are executed together now. In the earlier window, no trace contained A22 together with any of the four: about 47 of 100 traces took A22 alone, the remaining 53 took all four block activities. In the later window, every trace contains A22 and all four block activities. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- The block now runs directly after A20. In the earlier window, A20 always passed straight to A23 (all of A20's outgoing transitions went to A23, at event distance 1), and A23 and A21 always preceded the block. In the later window, A20 passes to one of the four block activities (about 19 to 29 of 100 transitions each), the block always precedes A23 and A21, and A20 reaches A23 only at event distance 5, with the four block events in between. [DIR001, LAG001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- The block's exit changed. In the earlier window, each of A31, A32, A37 and A38 led on to A26 in roughly 22 to 30 of 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window, they lead to A23 instead (about 22 to 29 of 100) and no longer directly to A26. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- A21 now always leads to A22. In the earlier window, about 47 of 100 of A21's outgoing transitions went to A22 and the rest to a block activity; in the later window, all go to A22, and the event distance from A21 to A26 is 2 in every trace, where before it was 2 on the A22 path and 5 on the block path. [DIR002, LAG002, REL012]
- The four block activities remain mutually unordered: in both windows, each pair among them occurs in both orders in roughly balanced shares, so no fixed order exists between them before or after. [REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- Relative event positions shifted accordingly: the block activities moved from a mean position of about 0.58 to about 0.40 of the trace, while A23 (about 0.39 to 0.47), A21 (about 0.54 to 0.61) and A22 (about 0.59 to 0.64) moved later; A20 sits slightly earlier (about 0.36 to 0.33) and A26 slightly later (about 0.64 to 0.66). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the exclusive branch between A22 and the four-activity block A31, A32, A37, A38 was replaced by a fixed sequence in which both are always executed: in the earlier window, each trace ran either A22 alone (about 47 of 100 traces) or the whole block (about 53 of 100) between A21 and A26, whereas in the later window A20 leads into the block, the block leads into A23, and A21 leads through A22 onward to A26, so every trace now contains both the block and A22. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002]

The support is direct and consistent: 52 evidence items qualified against fewer than 1 expected by chance across 116 screened units, so sampling noise cannot explain the pattern as a whole; the alternatives-together change is shown directly by co-occurrence rising from 0 to 100 of 100 traces, the relocation by order flips against A21 and A23 together with matching successor and distance changes, and every affected activity is well observed in both windows (about half of traces before, all traces after), which rules out an explanation resting on unobserved or rare behaviour. One competing reading the evidence cannot fully exclude is that this arose as two separate changes — the block becoming mandatory after A20 and A22 becoming mandatory after A21 — rather than a single restructuring of the branch point; the observed behaviour is the same under either reading, and differences below the reporting thresholds elsewhere in the process would not be visible. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, DIR001, LAG001, LAG002, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
